name: bg-particle-whirlpool

frames.best_why: Frame 4 shows a loose multicolour vortex with long magenta trails, the swirl at its clearest.

tagline: A swarm of neon sticks chases the cursor across black.
summary: A glowing cloud of hundreds of tiny coloured bars that swirl and cluster on a black stage, drifting toward wherever the pointer moves, with white copy over the lower centre.
appearance: On black, several hundred short glowing rectangular dashes in pink, green, cyan, yellow and white gather in a loose ball, denser at the middle and scattering to single sparks at the edges. A white title and lighter subtitle sit low in the frame.
behaviour: The dashes are pulled toward a moving target and settle into a rotating swarm, stretching along their travel direction. Moving the pointer relocates the attractor, and dragging the canvas swings the whole three-dimensional camera.
demo_content: The heading 'Particle Whirlpool' and the line 'Move your cursor and the swarm follows.'
search_phrases: physics particles that chase the cursor
bloom particle field for a hero
glowing dust that reacts to mouse
use_when: A launch or product page wants a lively, interactive particle swarm behind a headline.
avoid_when: Orbit controls stay active on the canvas, so a drag rotates the 3D camera instead of just moving the swarm.
customise: particleCount and blur are props and children render on top; camera distance, colouring, attraction and the bloom pass are set inside the source.
weight_why: Thousands of instanced meshes plus a full-screen bloom pass, redrawn every frame.

a11y.note: Decorative WebGL scene with no reduced-motion check, and its canvas also swallows drags through OrbitControls.

issues: The heading sits inside the densest particle cluster, so the title is partly covered in several frames.
OrbitControls stay live, so dragging the background rotates the camera unexpectedly.
polish_why: Bright, lively bloom swarm; the title is lost in the storm and drags rotate the camera.
title: Particle Whirlpool Background
